details.detail: Sidewall panel colour, finish and seams. The albedo #e9e7e2 matches the warm off-white in sans_14 (upper wall #f6f4eb) and R24 (#c3b6ac under warm light). Panel joints fall mid-pier after every second window, as in sans_14, where grooves sit between windows 2|3 and 4|5. In the assembled renders the upper half of every wall is washed saturated blue (see issues).

Window reveal proportions. The width is right: 0.39 m modelled against 0.37 m (132 px at 356 px/m in sans_14). F/J lower bowls are right: about 0.09-0.10 m below the opening in f_17313 and omaat Room-38, against 0.11 m modelled. PY/Y bowls are far too short: about 1.0 x the opening width (about 0.30 m) in both sans_14 and py_37303, against 0.11 m modelled. The reveal is also too shallow: the photos show a strong shading gradient into the opening (reveal top #b7b4a5 against wall #f6f4eb, 0.74), while the render is nearly flat.

F/J electric shades. The pleat count is right: about 37 pleats over the opening in R24 (FFT period 25 px over 915 px), against 40 modelled. The colour family is right. Pleat contrast is far too weak and the closed blackout is too bright relative to the bezel. The sheer's side edges show a sawtooth.

Shade button. The blue-ring split pill sits on the reveal sill directly under the opening. Its size (0.046 m tall) matches R24 (95 px against a 915 px opening, so about 0.046 m). The gap to the opening is 0.046 m in the model against about 0.032 m in the photo.

PY/Y manual shade. When stowed, the light grip lip shows at the top of the opening, as in sans_14, sans_24 and py_37301. The PY window has no button, which is correct (sans_24). The half and closed states look plausible, but no photo of a closed PY/Y shade was found.

Dado and grilles. Louvre count, rib count, rounded frame and white placards match py_37301 and py_37303. The grille proportions are wrong: 0.43 x 0.24 m (aspect 1.86, 56 % of the dado height) against about 0.33 x 0.30 m in the photos (aspect about 1.1, 78-84 % of the dado height). The in-cabin dado colour is over-saturated blue.
Y carpet and track covers. The Y aisle renders #4d5881, inside the photo range (#2f365b in y_47301 to #545d72 in y_47304). The royal-blue seat-track covers are now present.

F carpet. The first-class aisle renders mauve #887573, about 2x too bright. The photos show dark brown-charcoal: #423838 in f_17300, #2e2623 in the f_17313 footwell and #291f1c in the c_27312 aisle. carpetJ was raised for the J aisle and now blows out F.

Type A door linings and surrounds (doors 2 and 4). The door is a flat grey slab with a hard black outline, a small centred window, a thin vertical handle bar and a low, short bustle. The real ANA 777 door (sans_09, looking across at door 2) is warm off-white with no dark outline, a same-colour surround trim, a tall full-width slide bustle (about 40-45 % of the door height) and a red arc arming indicator above it.

Door-area and galley floor. It renders as light cool vinyl #a0a5ad. The ANA door-2 galley floor in sans_09 is a dark, warm, mottled stone-look grey (#666268 and #585353), darker than the galley cabinets (#8c8280).

Sun patches and window light on the wall. The patches are still thin diagonal streaks about 0.05 m wide across the seats (q14, q07), not pools of pane size. A new hard-edged rectangular bright box about 1.5 pitches wide appears on the wall round the nearest window (s05, s08).

issues.detail: [LIGHTING, affects the shell] Saturated blue wash over the upper sidewall and door linings in the default 'boarding' mood
issues.problem: In every assembled view, the wall from the bin line down to the middle of the windows is painted strong blue with a visible fade line. The door-2 and door-4 linings are blue as well. No boarding or daylight photo of this cabin shows this: the ANA official photos, sans_13 and sans_14 (boarding at HND) all show white walls and at most a thin cool line under the bins. The blue band exists only in the in-flight mood photos (sans_36, sans_39).
issues.evidence: Upper wall in the renders: s01 #7282ce (s 0.45), s02 #8c9ad9 (s 0.35), s08 #7081d5 (s 0.47), s05 #7485d6. In the photos: sans_14 upper wall #f6f4eb (s 0.04), y_47301 wall band #e2e5ec (s 0.05), py_37303 #9da8bb (s 0.16, whole-image cool cast). Measured in s05 col 400: luminance steps from 141 to 216 over y 140-180, a hard fade line.
issues.fix: Not in 07_shell.js. In 12_scene.js MOODS.boarding, set sideLed to a near-white low value, for example [0.10, 0.10, 0.11], or 0. Keep the blue band for 'cruise' only, and reduce it there to about [0.03, 0.03, 0.22]. In 04_shaders.js, cut the sideLed band term by about 0.8 on faces with layer 'door' / MAT.door so the door linings do not turn blue.

issues.detail: The PY/Y window reveal lower bowl is about 0.19 m too short
issues.problem: In PY and Y the 777 bathtub reveal continues about one opening-width (about 0.30 m) below the window opening, ending about 0.10-0.14 m above the dado. The model uses the short F/J bowl everywhere (REC.bot -0.33, 0.11 m below the opening). F/J are different: in f_17313 and omaat Room-38 the bowl ends about 0.09 m below the opening, so the current value is right there.
issues.evidence: py_37303: opening width about 65-95 px, bowl from the opening bottom y 110 to the reveal bottom y 200 = 90 px, gap to the dado top (y 243) 43 px. sans_14: opening ring 80 x 130 px, bowl 338 to 418 = 80 px, reveal bottom to the dado top about 30 px. In both, bowl/opening width is about 1.0, against 0.35 in the model. f_17313: bowl/opening width about 0.33. omaat Room-38: about 0.26.
issues.fix: In 07_shell.js, make REC per class: REC_J = REC (bot -0.33) for F/J windows and REC_Y = {...REC, bot: -0.52, rBot: 0.12} for PY/Y (reveal bottom at about 0.61 m above the floor, about 0.2 m above the dado top at 0.40). sdRecess/recessRay need to take the REC object. Build two windowCellPattern patterns (pat for electric windows, patY for manual ones) and choose per window in buildSidewallRun (pass w.electric through holesZ). WALL.bottomRows needs a row at 0.58 or lower so that the wall grid under the deeper bowl still meets the ring (it already has 0.58, and the ring corners define sideV). Build windowParts(side, patY) for the revealR/revealL instances of manual windows (split the instance lists into electric and manual). Do not move REC.btn for J.

issues.detail: The reveal is too shallow and flat-shaded; the photos show a deep funnel into the opening
issues.problem: In real photos the upper half of the reveal is visibly in shade as its surface turns in towards the opening (a soft grey gradient above the pane). In the renders the reveal floor is almost as bright as the wall, so the bathtub reads as a thin embossed outline.
issues.evidence: sans_14: the reveal just above the opening is #b7b4a5 against the wall pier/upper wall #f6f4eb (ratio 0.74), and the lower bowl is #d5d2c2 (0.87). s09 and s03 renders: the reveal floor above the opening is within about 5 % of the wall.
issues.fix: In 07_shell.js windowParts, raise REC.depth from 0.034 to about 0.060. Replace the single drafted wall ring with a sloped 'hood': add an intermediate ring, [inset(rec, 0.019), D*0.4] then [lerp toward scl(open,1.085) by 0.5, D*0.8], so the upper reveal surface faces down and inward. The deeper lip and hood then shade naturally under the hemi term. Move SHADE.depth accordingly (REC.depth + 0.046 already follows).

issues.detail: Dado grille proportions: too wide and too short
issues.problem: The modelled grille is a letterbox 0.43 x 0.24 m (with frame) that almost fills the window pitch and only 56 % of the dado height. The photos show a squarer grille, about 0.33 wide x 0.30 tall, filling about 80 % of the dado height, with clear dado panel and a placard between grilles.
issues.evidence: py_37303 (zoomed, 3x): grille 71 x 64 px (aspect 1.1), dado top to floor about 82 px, so the grille fills 78 %. py_37301 crop: grille height 310 px of a 370 px dado, 84 %. sans_14: visible grille about 65 x 60 px. Model: ghw 0.205, ghh 0.112 (plus a 0.012 frame): aspect 1.86, 0.224/0.40 = 56 %.
issues.fix: In 07_shell.js windowParts, set ghw 0.205 -> 0.160, ghh 0.112 -> 0.135 and gc 0.19 -> 0.195, so the grille spans v 0.06-0.33 inside the 0.05-0.33 facet (clip the frame at the DADO knee 0.33 or lift DADO[2] to 0.345). Scale nSl 30 -> 36 to keep the slat pitch, and the ribs 9 -> 7. Move the placard (lb, lz = W.pitch/2 - 0.006) so it sits in the now wider gap.

issues.detail: Dado renders an over-saturated royal blue in the cabin
issues.problem: After the r2 albedo lift, the in-cabin dado reads #293666 (hue 228, s 0.60), a saturated blue. The photos show a desaturated slate (#455162, s 0.30), with the grille (#2e3643) darker than the panel.
issues.evidence: s04_dadoLow: dado #293666 and grille #293044 (the same luminance, so no panel/louvre contrast). py_37303: dado #455162, grille #2e3643.
issues.fix: In 07_shell.js MAT.dado, desaturate: c '#6c7690' -> '#6f7584' (keep the luminance, cut the blue). Check whether the lighting ambient (hemiBot / sideLed) is adding blue at floor level. Lower MAT.grille '#707b96' -> '#5d6474' so the louvre field averages darker than the panel.

issues.detail: The F carpet renders mauve and about 2x too bright
issues.problem: F zones share MAT.carpetJ, which was pushed to #645554 to fix a too-dark J aisle between tall shells. In the open F aisle it now renders a light pinkish mauve, which no photo shows.
issues.fix: In 07_shell.js MAT, add carpetF: { c: '#4a3e39', r: 0.95, l: LAYER.fabric } (warm brown-charcoal, hue about 15) and use it in the buildShell floor loop when zn.cls === 'F'. Shift carpetJ's hue from plum to brown: '#645554' -> '#5e5049', or compensate the J aisle darkness in lighting rather than in albedo.

issues.detail: Closed electric shades: pleat contrast is too weak and the blackout is too light against the bezel
issues.problem: In R24 the closed pleated blackout shows strong alternating crest and valley bands and sits clearly darker than the reveal bezel. The model bakes only x0.86 into the valley rows, so closed shades read as nearly plain slabs.
issues.evidence: omaat Room-24 column profile through the shade: p10/p90 = 75/163 (valley about 0.46 of crest). Shade mean #787367 against bezel #bdb4a9 (0.64). Model: valley x0.86; MAT.blackout #cbc7bf against MAT.reveal #e7e4dd (0.87).
issues.fix: In 07_shell.js shadePanelGeo, change the valley multiplier 0.86 -> 0.62 (blackout) and 0.80 (sheer, which is backlit). Lower MAT.blackout c '#cbc7bf' -> '#b4ada2'. Optionally raise the zig-zag zz 0.005 -> 0.007 so the pleat normals shade more.

issues.detail: Type A door lining (doors 2-4): black outline, short bustle, and a handle and window layout that do not match the ANA door
issues.problem: The door reads as a flat grey panel outlined in black. The real ANA 777 door lining is warm off-white, and its perimeter is a soft same-colour trim, not a dark line. Its slide bustle is a tall full-width box covering about 40-45 % of the door height, with a red arc arming indicator above it. The model's bustle is 0.36 m tall (about 19 %) and it has a thin vertical silver handle and a small red flag near the top.
issues.evidence: sans_09 (crop sans09_door): door header about y 220, floor about 850 in the 3x crop; the bustle box spans y 570-850 (44 %); red arc at y 450-560; no dark perimeter line. s06/s07: 12 mm MAT.doorGap outline strips, and the MAT.slide box 0.36 tall centred at v 0.30.
issues.fix: Door leaf details are in 10_mono.js (the Type A door lining block), and the surround is in 07_shell.js buildShell (the door-surround windowCell, MAT.door). In 07_shell.js MAT, set doorGap '#2a2d31' -> '#9a968e' (a shadowed seam, not black) and door '#dddbd5' -> '#e3ddd2'. In 10_mono.js (monument owner), make the outline strips 4 mm wide and inset 2 mm. Change the MAT.slide gRBox from (0.10, 0.36, 0.92) at v 0.30 to (0.12, 0.78, 0.98) at v 0.41. Replace the red flag with a red arc (a gTube half-circle of radius 0.10 m) at v 0.90. Change the handle to a horizontal lever about 0.35 m long at v 1.0.

issues.detail: Door-area and galley floor vinyl is too light and cool
issues.problem: MAT.vinyl #8d9096 renders light blue-grey (#a0a5ad at door 2), brighter than the galley cabinets. ANA's door-2 galley floor is a dark warm grey with a mottled stone look.
issues.evidence: sans_09: floor #666268 and #585353 (mottled), cabinets #8c8280 (floor/cabinet about 0.7). s06: floor #a0a5ad.
issues.fix: In 07_shell.js MAT, set vinyl { c: '#6b6664', r: 0.5, l: LAYER.vinyl }, and make sure LAYER.vinyl has a low-frequency mottle (about 0.2-0.4 m blotches, ±12 % luminance). The LAYER_PARAMS change is a shared-file edit in 03_tex.js.

issues.detail: [LIGHTING/SHELL] Hard-edged rectangular bright box on the wall around the nearest window
issues.problem: In the jShades and pyShades close views, a rectangle about 1.5 window pitches wide is uniformly brighter than the surrounding wall, with vertical edges one pixel sharp. It looks like an AO-volume cell or window-glow footprint rather than light.
issues.evidence: s05 row 200: RGB about (184,191,223) left of x 420, (221,226,237) inside, stepping sharply at x about 420 and about 820; row 150: 148 to 180. The same box shows in s08 round the window at x 330-560.
issues.fix: Owned by lighting (04_shaders.js window-glow / AO-volume sampling): use trilinear AO sampling and a smooth falloff on the per-window glow footprint. Shell side: make sure the window glow reads the reveal normals (ring 0 normals already copy the wall normal) and not a box extent.

issues.detail: Sun patches through the windows are still thin streaks
issues.problem: Direct sun through a 10 x 15 in pane should make a patch at least pane-wide. The renders show 0.03-0.06 m wide diagonal bands across seats and wood.
issues.evidence: q14 seat backs: bright bands about 20-30 px wide at about 1.5 m; q07: a diagonal band across the ash panel.
issues.fix: Shadow-map / sun-LUT issue: check that the window glass (castShadow false) and the reveal lining are not both culling the light, so that only the gap between the lining and the shade rail lets sun through. In 07_shell.js set castShadow:false on the reveal mesh 'reveal'+key, and let the sun LUT use the pane rectangle (W.w x W.h).

issues.detail: Sawtooth edge on the sheer shade
issues.problem: The sheer's 5 mm zig-zag pleat ends show as a jagged vertical edge at the side of the opening, where the lining necks down.
issues.evidence: s05_jShades left window at x about 215, y 200-430.
issues.fix: In 07_shell.js SHADE, widen w 0.320 -> 0.335 so the ends hide behind the lining (scl(open, 0.986) half-width about 0.150), or add a 6 mm side hem strip (gBox) at ±w/2 in shadePanelGeo.

issues.detail: The shade button sits slightly too low under the opening
issues.problem: The pill centre is 0.046 m below the opening bottom; R24 shows about 0.032 m.
issues.evidence: omaat Room-24: opening bottom y 985, pill centre y 1050, opening height 915 px (0.445 m), so 0.032 m.

questionsForUser: The upper sidewall is washed saturated blue in the default 'Boarding' mood. ANA's boarding and daylight photos (sans_13/14, all official photos) show white walls, and the blue only appears in in-flight mood photos. Should boarding be white, with the blue band only in Cruise?

Reveal height above the opening. Both high-camera photos (sans_14, f_17313) show the reveal rising about 1.4 x the opening width above the opening, which would put its top at about 1.75 m, above the modelled bin line at 1.60 m. Do you have an eye-level photo of the PY/Y wall, or an ANA 777 sidewall drawing, to set the bin-line height (WALL.vTop) and REC.top?
Is the door-area floor between the galleys carpet or dark mottled vinyl? sans_09 (door 2) shows vinyl in the galley, but the cross-aisle at the door itself is too dark to tell.

No clear ANA photo of a Type A door lining close up was found; sans_09 shows door 2 only from across the galley. Can you supply one (L2, L3 or L4) so the bustle height, handle and arming indicator can be verified?
